title: Secure a Self-Custody Wallet Before Funding It
hook: The seed phrase is not a password reset. It is control of the asset.
outcome: A compartmentalized wallet setup with tested recovery.
steps: Choose a wallet whose code, reputation, supported networks, and recovery model you understand.
Create it on a clean device. Never photograph, cloud-sync, email, or paste the seed phrase into a website.
Store recovery material offline in separate secure locations and test recovery with an empty wallet.
Use separate wallets for storage, transactions, experiments, and public identity.
Send a small test transaction, verify addresses on trusted displays, and review approvals regularly.
cta: Save this before moving funds on-chain.
disclaimer: Digital assets can be lost permanently and may be highly volatile. Educational only, not investment advice.

title: Read the Contract Before You Trust the Website
hook: A polished interface can point to dangerous or upgradeable code.
outcome: A practical smart-contract risk review before interacting.
steps: Confirm the exact chain and contract address through multiple trusted sources.
Check whether source code is verified and whether the deployed bytecode matches.
Inspect owner privileges, upgradeability, pause controls, minting, fees, allowlists, oracles, and withdrawal paths.
Review audits, disclosed issues, bug bounties, admin-key controls, and changes since the audit.
Simulate the transaction, limit approvals, use a low-value wallet, and monitor resulting permissions.
cta: Comment CONTRACT for the review checklist.
disclaimer: Audits and verified code do not guarantee safety. Smart-contract interactions can be irreversible.

title: What Tokenizing a Real-World Asset Actually Requires
hook: A token does not automatically create ownership, cash flow, or legal enforceability.
outcome: A reality-first map from underlying asset to rights, compliance, custody, and reporting.
steps: Identify the actual asset, owner, jurisdiction, liabilities, cash flows, and transfer restrictions.
Define exactly what the token represents: access, a claim, equity, debt, revenue share, or something else.
Map securities, money-transmission, tax, consumer, property, privacy, and identity requirements.
Design custody, servicing, governance, defaults, redemptions, records, and dispute handling.
Connect on-chain supply to off-chain evidence and independent reporting.
cta: Share this with anyone calling a token 'the asset.'
disclaimer: Tokenization can involve complex securities, property, tax, custody, and financial-services laws. Obtain qualified legal advice.
